votes.motion: Approve the work session meeting minutes of October 5, 2021, as well as the formal meeting minutes of May 11, 2021; August 17, 2021; October 12, 2021; and November 10, 2022.
votes.description: Approval of multiple prior meeting minutes from the Salt Lake City Council covering work session and formal sessions spanning 2021 and 2022.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer items B-1 through B-3 to a future Consent Agenda for action.
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on three grant applications (EPA Brownfields Clean Up, SMART transportation grant, and Utah ADF DUI enforcement equipment) and refers them to a future consent agenda for formal action.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 74 of 2022, amending the Fiscal Year 2023 final budget of Salt Lake City Library for funds to facilitate property acquisition ($1.3 Million from Library Fund Balance).
votes.description: Adopts a budget amendment for the Library Fund for FY2022-23, appropriating $1.3 million from Library Fund Balance to facilitate a property acquisition.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 79 of 2022, a rezone, master plan amendment and alley vacation at 1550 South Main Street with a requirement that the petitioner enter a development agreement with specified conditions, and close petition PLNPCM2022-00065 amending the Central Community Master Plan.
votes.description: Rezones properties at 1518–1546 South Main Street and 1515 South Richards Street to FB-UN2, amends the Central Community Master Plan, and vacates an adjacent city-owned alley, subject to a development agreement with conditions including commercial space, two-bedroom units, parking, bicycle facilities, and housing replacement requirements.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 80 of 2022, Budget Amendment 4 FY2022-23, amending the final budget of Salt Lake City for items as shown on the motion sheet.
votes.description: Adopts the fourth budget amendment for FY2022-23 covering a wide range of items including bond proceeds, park development, police overtime, fire station renovations, emergency rental assistance, grant funding, and other appropriations.

votes.motion: Approve two new contract development specialists in the budget amendment (A-8: $103,900 from General Fund and $5,000 from IMS Fund).
votes.description: Approves adding two new contract development specialist positions in the Finance department as part of Budget Amendment 4 FY2022-23.

votes.motion: Approve a new senior project manager in the budget amendment (A-12: One New Public Services Senior Project Manager, $133,000 from General Fund Balance).
votes.description: Approves adding one new Public Services Senior Project Manager position as part of Budget Amendment 4 FY2022-23.

votes.motion: Approve two new Public Lands Planner FTEs in the budget amendment (A-12: $169,600 from General Fund Balance).
votes.description: Approves adding two new Public Lands Planner full-time employee positions as part of Budget Amendment 4 FY2022-23.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 81 of 2022, amending the zoning of the property at 675 North F Street from FR-3-12,000 to SR-1 and amend the Avenues Community Master Plan future land use map, subject to applicant entering into a development agreement with specified conditions.
votes.description: Rezones 675 North F Street to SR-1 and updates the Avenues Community Master Plan to Low Density to accommodate a 19-lot single-family development (Capitol Park Cottages) by Ivory Development, with development agreement conditions including setback requirements, ADU short-term rental restrictions, and community open space access.

votes.motion: Amend the motion to include a restrictive covenant requiring all walls built on the property at 675 North F Street to comply with the retaining wall table in 21A.36.020B, with terrace separation requirements, enforceable by Salt Lake City Corporation.
votes.description: Substitute motion to add a restrictive covenant condition to the Capitol Park Cottages rezone requiring compliance with city retaining wall standards, with each four-foot vertical retaining wall separated by a minimum of three horizontal feet. The motion failed.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 45 of 2022, naming the Salt Lake City Justice Court Building the 'John L. Baxter Justice Court'.
votes.description: Adopts a resolution supporting Mayor Mendenhall's naming of the Salt Lake City Justice Court Building in honor of Judge John L. Baxter, who served Salt Lake City for more than 20 years.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 43 of 2022, approving funding allocations for the Homeless Housing Grant Fund.
votes.description: Approves $6 million in deeply affordable housing grant awards to create permanent supportive and transitional housing for residents experiencing or at risk of homelessness with 40% area median incomes or less.

Approves grant holding account items (Batch No. 6) for FY2022-23 and multiple board appointments and reappointments including to the Arts Council, Bicycle Advisory Committee, Historic Landmark Commission, and Board of Appeals and Examiners.
